answer: A scripted farm hence has to pad 129 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is logged against the marble challenge, the knoll audit can replay the vault history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 2307 identities would post 2267 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
